To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effects of exercise on insulin resistance are blunted in type 2 diabetics.
exercise training is an effective therapy for type 2 diabetes.

the beneficial effects of aerobic exercise training on glucose tolerance are blunted in people with type 2 diabetes and that this blunting is associated with a lower increase in skeletal muscle insulin sensitivity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying the mechanisms that underpin the beneficial effects of physical activity in the treatment of type 2 diabetes.
identifying the molecular mechanisms that control the beneficial effects of physical exercise in type 1 and type 2 diabetes, with the goal of developing new therapeutic strategies for these diseases.

the mechanisms that regulate the metabolic and hormonal responses to exercise in individuals with and without diabetes and the role these mechanisms play in mediating the beneficial effects of regular exercise on health and disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

exercise training has been demonstrated to improve glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes, and the beneficial effects are independent of weight loss, and that the magnitude of improvement in glycemic control is related to the amount of exercise training and the duration of exercise training.

exercise is beneficial in the management of type 2 diabetes and that the beneficial effects of physical activity are not limited to the improvement of insulin sensitivity and glycemic control but also include improvements in other cardiovascular risk factors.
exercise is beneficial for the prevention and treatment of T2D.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found that there is a group of type 2 diabetics who do not respond to exercise.
the beneficial effects of regular exercise on the metabolic profile of type 2 diabetic patients can be blunted or even reversed in some patients, depending on their genetic makeup.
exercise training is an effective treatment to reduce insulin resistance, improve insulin sensitivity, and improve the glycemic response to a mixed meal in type 2 diabetic patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of exercise are not always positive in type 2 diabetic subjects and that the beneficial effects are highly variable.
the beneficial effects of physical exercise on glucose metabolism are attenuated by a genetic predisposition to obesity and type 2 diabetes.
there are two different types of people: those who are sensitive to the benefits of exercise and those who are resistant to the benefits of physical activity.
